defects.description: The rules file allows only yyyy-MM-dd with hyphens and lists 1985/07/14 as a rejected example. The AUT accepts a slash-separated date: POST /contacts with birthdate '1985/07/14' returns 201 and stores '1985/07/14' verbatim; the Add Contact page also saves it and goes to the Contact List. Other wrong layouts (07/14/1985, 1985-7-14, 1985.01.01) and impossible dates (1985-02-30, 1985-13-01) are correctly rejected.
defects.evidence: POST /contacts {firstName:'Jane',lastName:'Doe',birthdate:'1985/07/14'} -> 201 {..."birthdate":"1985/07/14"...} (probed 3 times, plus '1980/01/01' -> 201 on POST, PUT and PATCH). UI: Add Contact with Date of Birth 1985/07/14 -> redirected to /contactList, no error. Controls: '07/14/1985' -> 400 'Contact validation failed: birthdate: Birthdate is invalid'.

defects.description: The rules file lists '+44 7911 123456' (15 characters, international number with spaces) as an accepted phone example. The AUT rejects it with 400 'Contact validation failed: phone: Phone number is invalid', and the Add Contact page shows that error, although the same number without spaces (+447911123456) and '+1 800 555 1234' (also 15 characters with spaces) are accepted.
defects.evidence: POST /contacts {firstName:'Jane',lastName:'Doe',phone:'+44 7911 123456'} -> 400 {"message":"Contact validation failed: phone: Phone number is invalid"} (probed 3 times). UI: Phone '+44 7911 123456' -> stays on /addContact, #error 'Contact validation failed: phone: Phone number is invalid'. Controls: '+1 800 555 1234' -> 201, '+447911123456' -> 201.

traps: Postal code boundary: a 10-character value must be a real postal-code shape (12345-6789 -> 201). '1234567890' (10 digits) is rejected with 'Postal code is invalid' - that is a format rejection of a value that is not a postal code, not a max-length defect. 11 characters -> 400 '...maximum allowed length (10)' (met).

Phone boundary: '+1 800 555 1234' (15 chars) -> 201; '+1 800 555 12345' (16) -> 400 max length. A made-up 15-digit string like '123456789012345' is rejected as 'Phone number is invalid' (the validator is a real-phone-number check); do not report that as a max-length defect - the CSV example to test is '+44 7911 123456' (D2).

Only the listed examples have a guaranteed outcome; the phone validator is locale-based and rejects some odd digit strings (e.g. 13-14 plain digits, '555-1234'). Improvised values outside the CSV examples are not evidence of a deviation.

The mock-up PNG is the oracle for AC-1/AC-2: labels '* First Name:', '* Last Name:', 'Date of Birth:' (placeholder yyyy-MM-dd), 'Email:' (example@email.com), 'Phone:' (8005551234), 'Street Address 1:', 'Street Address 2:', 'City:', 'State or Province:', 'Postal Code:', 'Country:'; list columns Name, Birthdate, Email, Phone, Address, 'City, State/Province, Postal Code', Country. All match the live app.
UI error text is the full API message, e.g. 'Contact validation failed: birthdate: Birthdate is invalid' - AC-3 only requires that it contains the CSV error text.
AC numbering: the story has no ids; the 7 'The system shall' paragraphs are AC-1..AC-7 in order (AC-5 = CSV rules on POST /contacts, AC-3 = UI rejection).
Leading/trailing spaces are trimmed for all text fields (firstName, lastName, city, email, country verified) - AC-6 met.
The UI stores the token in a cookie and the contact list reloads via GET /contacts on page load; a contact created by API appears after reload (met).
No data-testid attributes; use element ids (#add-contact, #firstName, ..., #submit, #error, tr.contactTableBodyRow).
expectations: AC-1 PASS: Add a New Contact -> /addContact with labels/placeholders as in the mock-up; '*' on first/last name.
AC-2 PASS: valid submit -> /contactList, row 'Jane Doe | 1985-07-14 | jane.doe@example.com | 8005551234 | 1 Main St. Apartment A | Anytown KS 12345 | USA'.
AC-3 FAIL only through D1/D2 in the UI (slash date saved; +44 phone refused); the other rejected examples keep the user on /addContact with the error text.
AC-4 PASS: 201 with _id, all sent values and owner = signed-in user's _id.
AC-5 FAIL (D1, D2); every other accepted/rejected example in the CSV behaves as written (verified one by one, including 20/21, 40/41 and 20/21 boundaries).
AC-7 PASS: UI-added contact is returned by GET /contacts with the same values; API-created contact appears in the UI list after reload.
